minor.title: Forgot-password rate limit is per-IP only — no per-email bucket
minor.description:
The Round-1 recommendation called for BOTH a per-email key (forgot:rate:{email} 60s, primary defence against email-bombing a single known victim) AND a per-IP counter (secondary, for clearly abusive volumes). The implemented mitigation only sets forgot:rate:ip:{ip} TTL=60s. An attacker with access to a small pool of IPs (or a residential-proxy / botnet rotation) can still flood any one victim's inbox: each IP can fire one request per minute, so N IPs ⇒ N reset emails per minute to the same target. CGNAT users behind shared IPs are also penalised in the other direction — one user's reset blocks every other user behind that NAT for 60s.

Note: the per-IP-only fix DOES close the SMTP-egress-abuse vector at single-attacker scale, and DOES bound the audit-log write rate. So this is a partial fix, not a regression — flagging as minor because it's strictly weaker than the spec'd defence-in-depth.
minor.impact: Email-bombing of a known victim's inbox is still feasible from a multi-IP attacker (low-skill if the attacker rents residential proxies). Pending-token DoS (overwriting in-flight reset tokens) is still possible at lower rate. Outbound SMTP volume is bounded per IP but not in aggregate.

minor.category: OWASP A09 - Security Logging and Monitoring (test coverage)
minor.title: Timing-parity fix has no automated regression assertion
minor.description:
Round-1 finding #2 recommended adding an automated assertion (unit timing or IT) to catch future regressions of the FORGOT_DUMMY_DELAY. The fix landed (40ms Mono.delay on the unknown/deleted/blocked branch) but no test asserts that both branches take comparable wall-clock time. Anyone refactoring AuthService.doForgotPassword in the future could remove the delay without any test failing — and the next security-auditor pass would have to re-discover the timing oracle by hand.

This is not an exploitable vulnerability today; it is a test-coverage gap that materially weakens the durability of the fix.
minor.impact: Future maintainers may silently regress the timing-oracle defence. Detection delay = next manual security review.
minor.recommendation:
Add a coarse timing assertion. Two cheap options:

(a) Use VirtualTimeScheduler in StepVerifier to verify the unknown-email branch DOES emit a Mono.delay subscription:
  StepVerifier.withVirtualTime(() -> authService.forgotPassword("ghost@x", exchange()))
      .expectSubscription()
      .expectNoEvent(Duration.ofMillis(40))
      .verifyComplete();

(b) An IT-level wall-clock comparison with high tolerance (e.g. abs(t_known - t_unknown) < 100ms over 5 samples). More flaky in CI; option (a) preferred.

Either test pinned to the FORGOT_DUMMY_DELAY constant catches removal regressions.

minor.category: OWASP A04 - Insecure Design (carry-over from Round 1)
minor.title: Reset token transported as URL query parameter — frontend mitigations still pending
minor.description: Re-flagged from Round-1 finding #6 per orchestrator's note. The reset-password.html template still emits {APP_URL}/auth/reset-password?token={TOKEN}. Backend implementation is fine; the mitigations are frontend-side (Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on the reset page, history.replaceState to strip the token from the URL after extraction). Flagging here as a tracking note so the frontend epic does not lose sight of it — NOT blocking for Task 6 acceptance.
minor.location: backend/src/main/resources/templates/email/reset-password.html:12 (token in query string) — frontend mitigation lives outside this task
minor.impact: If the reset-password page loads any third-party resource (analytics, fonts, images) OR if a user shares / pastes / has the URL captured in webserver logs within the 1h TTL, the token is recoverable. Window is bounded by TTL and HTTPS in transit.
minor.recommendation: Frontend epic: (a) <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer"> or HTTP Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on /auth/reset-password page; (b) immediately after extracting the token client-side, call history.replaceState({}, '', '/auth/reset-password') so the token is not retained in browser history.

round1Verification.major1_rateLimitOnForgotPassword: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — per-IP key implemented (forgot:rate:ip:{ip} TTL=60s, fail-open per Decision 4, silent over-limit drop preserves anti-enumeration). Per-email key NOT implemented; downgraded to minor (see findings).
round1Verification.major2_timingOracle: RESOLVED — Mono.delay(FORGOT_DUMMY_DELAY=40ms) on unknown/deleted/blocked branch equalises wall-clock with the known-user save+email-build path. No regression assertion landed; downgraded to minor (see findings).
round1Verification.minor3_metadataAsymmetry: RESOLVED — both branches now pass null metadata to eventService.logEvent. Tests forgotPassword_unknownEmail_*WithNullMetadata and forgotPassword_deletedUser_*WithNullMetadata assert eq(null).
round1Verification.minor4_piiInLogs: RESOLVED — log.warn now emits userId instead of email on dispatch failure (line 305-306).
round1Verification.minor5_constantTimeHashCompare: ACCEPTED AS-IS — defense-in-depth note only at 256-bit entropy; orchestrator confirms.
round1Verification.minor6_tokenInUrlQuery: DEFERRED to frontend epic — re-flagged as a minor tracking note.
round1Verification.minor7_hardcodedTestPassword: ACCEPTED AS-IS — pre-existing, not Task 6 scope; orchestrator confirms.
bonusFixesObserved: Status gate added to resetPassword (lines 334-337): blocked/deleted users cannot rotate password even with valid unexpired token. Tests resetPassword_blockedUser_*_doesNotRotate and resetPassword_deletedUser_*_doesNotRotate cover both. This addresses an account-lifecycle invariant the original spec did not call out.
@Size(max=254) on ForgotPasswordRequest.email defends against pathological-length inputs that survive @Email/@NotBlank.
Pending users still allowed to reset (forgot password before email verification is a normal flow) — explicit and documented in code comment line 281-282.

findings.title: Forgot-password rate limit is per-IP only — no per-email bucket
findings.description: Per-IP-only rate limit allows email-bombing of a single victim from a multi-IP attacker (residential-proxy rotation) at N requests/min where N = number of distinct source IPs. CGNAT users penalise each other.
findings.impact: Email-bombing victim possible at scale; pending-token DoS still feasible at lower rate.
findings.recommendation: Add complementary forgot:rate:email:{email} key alongside the per-IP key, both checked before the user lookup. Silent over-limit, fail-open on Redis error.

findings.impact: Defence durability — future regressions only caught by next manual security review.

findings.title: Reset token transported as URL query parameter
findings.description: Frontend epic concern: token in URL retained in browser history and leaks via Referer to third-party resources. Backend OK; flagging for frontend tracking.
findings.impact: Token recoverable within 1h TTL if URL is leaked.
findings.recommendation: Frontend: Referrer-Policy: no-referrer + history.replaceState to remove token after extraction.
